title: WHAT IS THIS YOU ARE DOING?

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"When his father-in-law saw all that Moses was doing for the people, he said,
'What is this you are doing for the people? Why do you alone sit as judge, while
all these people stand around you from morning till evening?'"
- Ex 18:14 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Jethro watches for one day and asks a question.

It takes an outsider to see it. Moses had been living inside this pattern for so
long that it had become normal to him. Jethro arrived with fresh eyes and
immediately saw what everyone else had stopped noticing.

That is one of the great values of people who are outside our daily situation.
They ask the obvious question that those of us inside it have stopped asking.

Notice how Jethro asks. He does not accuse Moses of pride or empire-building.
He asks what is happening and why. He is genuinely curious before he is
corrective. Good counsel usually begins with a question rather than a verdict.

Notice also that Jethro noticed the people, not only Moses. "All these people
stand around you from morning till evening." He saw the cost on both sides: an
exhausted leader and a queue of people not being served well.

Proverbs says, "Wounds from a friend can be trusted" (Prov 27:6). Jethro was
about to say something Moses would not enjoy hearing.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Who in your life is close enough to ask you a hard question?
2. Have you stopped noticing something because it has become normal?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, give me people who love me enough to ask hard questions, and give me the
humility to hear them. Amen.
